INTRODUCTION "Pace Car Pro" is the first racing game in which four players can share in the excitement of a simulated high speed race. The game has been designed to provide the same excitement for one, two, three, or four players, since a "robot" pace car provides built-in competition. To add to the excitement, there are realistic motor sounds (one for each car), crash sounds, an infield that actually causes the cars to "slow" down, anda "joy- stick" control for each car that controls speed, direction, and braking. When set for single coin per player pricing, Pace Car Pro has the potential to increase income. It is the first game with the capability of taking in one dollar per play. Each "Pace Car Pro" game undergoes hours of testing before it is judged acceptac! for shipment. Thorough component testing involving thermal cycling, final inspec and testing - 24 hour operative testing of individual electronic assemblies and color television, and finally a 24 hour test for the complete game. Every game must pass all tests before it can be shipped. The game has been designed with ease of servicing in mind. All electronic p.c. modules and the color television are accessible by removing the cabinet top. The entire game electronics is contained on two plug-in logic printed circui: ards, a plug-in power supply board, and a color adjust board. Despite all testing and precautions taken, malfunctions sometimes occur. Refer to the trouble-shooting guide to isolate the problem, and contact tho distributor from whom the game was purchased for repair or replacement instructions. "Do not attempt to perform repairs on any in-warranty printed electronics boards, as the warranty will be voided."

Except as hereinafter stated, Electra Games, Inc., warrants the color television and the modular electronic printed circuit boards used in "Pace Car Pro" to be free from defects in material or workmanship under normal use. Access into the Base 1s necessary to reach the Cash Box, Coin Chute, Power Cord, or to remove the Control Panel. 2) Removal of the Top allows access to all of the Electronics Modules, Coin Equipment, and the Color Television. The keys to the Top are also located in the Instruction Manual envelope. 3) Removal of the Control Panel is only necessary for access to the "Joysticks" or for additional door opening clearance. GENERAL: The Pace Car (green blip) serves a two-fold purpose: ND) It performs the function of a “built-in” opponent making it possible for one person to pley. 2) It operates as a Game Timer which determines the duration of each play (race). The four opponent cars are the Red, Yellow, Violet, and Blue blips. These cars are controlled by the four color keyed "Joysticks" on the front panel. Eack "Joystick" controls the Speed, Direction, and Braking of its respective car. The "Joystick" is mechanically biased to return to center position. The four ‘Lap Counters (color keyed to each car) show the Progress of each c:: advancing - one count - for each completed lap. One lap is completed wne car is moved counter-clockwise from the Starting line, completely around t>s track and back to the starting line, (in Play Condition) . The Pace Car laps are indicated py "Hash" Marks displayed just below the Lap Counters. The total pace car laps to be completed are shown at the b. of the race, and then one is subtracted tor each lap completed by the Pace until the race ends. The "Joystick" Amciifier Adjustment is factory set and normally require readjustment only when the the EG1000-A Analog Board is changed, or if any of the "Joysticks" are replaced. There are two controls for each car. The controls adjust the voltage at the output of the "Joystick" Amplifiers.
